title: Correct capacitor charge
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final answer for part (1) must be numerically correct, approximately 6.4 × 10⁻⁵ C.

title: Correct charge through R₂
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final answer for part (2) must be numerically correct, approximately 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ C.

title: Apply Ohm's Law correctly
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the current in the circuit using the total EMF and the total resistance in the loop containing the source and R₃.

title: Relate capacitor voltage to R₃
description: Important Criteria: The student must recognize that the voltage across the capacitor equals the voltage across resistor R₃ when the switch is closed.

title: Apply charge conservation
description: Important Criteria: For part (2), the student must apply the principle of charge conservation, recognizing the total capacitor discharge splits equally between the two parallel branches containing R₁ and R₂.

title: Unit consistency and conversion
description: Optional Criteria: The student's work should correctly handle units, particularly converting microfarads to farads for capacitance calculations.

title: Misidentify capacitor voltage
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly assumes the capacitor voltage is the source EMF or the voltage across a different resistor.

title: Incorrect discharge path analysis
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly analyzes the discharge path after opening the switch, failing to recognize the parallel split of current between R₁ and R₂.
